title: Flat base change for proper global sections
statement: Let $R$ be a ring, let $f:X\to\operatorname{Spec}R$ be proper, and let $R\to R'$ be a flat ring map with $U=\operatorname{Spec}R'$ and $X_U=X\times_{\operatorname{Spec}R}U$. The canonical base-change map $H^0(X,\mathcal O_X)\otimes_RR'\to H^0(X_U,\mathcal O_{X_U})$ is an isomorphism. In particular, if $H^0(X,\mathcal O_X)=R$, then $H^0(X_U,\mathcal O_{X_U})=R'$.

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, Lemma 30.5.2 (Tag 02KH, label coherent-lemma-flat-base-change-cohomology), the quasi-compact quasi-separated flat-base-change lemma specialized here to the proper morphism and degree $0$, used in the proof of More on Morphisms Theorem 37.53.5

proof.text: Apply the general flat-base-change theorem [lem-pc-flat-base-change-cohom] to the cartesian square obtained from f:X -> Spec R and Spec R' -> Spec R, with the quasi-coherent sheaf F = O_X and i=0. Proper morphisms are quasi-compact and quasi-separated, so its hypotheses hold; the pullback of O_X is O_{X_U}. The theorem identifies the canonical map H^0(X,O_X) tensor_R R' -> H^0(X_U,O_{X_U}) with an isomorphism. If H^0(X,O_X)=R, then R tensor_R R' is canonically R', giving the final assertion.
